in_arabic.name: داولت
in_arabic.long_meaning: داولت هو مصدر من أصول عربية، يعني الحكم والمال والسلطة. يُستخدم هذا الاسم لتسمية الأطفال في عدة ثقافات إسلامية بسبب تواجده في القرآن الكريم، حيث يذكر في سورة الشورى: { وَأَنَّا لِلَّهِ وَلِرَسُولِهِ الْحُكْمُ } [الشورى: 40]. يحمل الاسم داولت معانٍ متعددة، منها: الحكم، والسلطة، والمال، والسيطرة. في عدة ثقافات إسلامية، يُعتبر الاسم داولت من أهم الأسماء في التسمية للأطفال، حيث يُعتبر بمعنى الحكم أو السلطة، مما يجعله مناسبًا لتسمية أطفال من ذوي المسميات الحكومية أو السياسية.

in_english.long_meaning: Daulat is an Arabic-derived name that means governance, power, wealth, and control. The name is significant in Islamic culture and is often used as a name for children. The name conveys multiple meanings, including governance, power, wealth, and control. In Islamic tradition, the name is derived from the Arabic root dal-aw-l, which carries the meanings of governance, power, and wealth. The name is mentioned in the Quran, specifically in Surah Al-Shura, verse 40, which states, "And that we decree to the sovereignty of Allah and to his messenger the judgment." The name Daulat is often chosen by parents for their children due to its association with governance and power.

data.cultural_impact: The name "Daulat" holds significant historical relevance in Islamic culture. It was the name of the Mughal Empire in India, established in 1526, and was used to denote the political power held by the Emperor. The ruler was seen as the representative of God on earth and was responsible for maintaining law and order according to Islamic principles. Daulat also refers to the fortune or wealth of a person, emphasizing the importance of hard work and just rulership for prosperity.
data.spiritual_significance: In a spiritual sense, "Daulat" represents the ultimate and absolute authority of Allah (God) over all things. historical_references.reference: Historical records show that Ibn Khaldun's Muqaddimah The name Daulat carried significant weight in that era.
historical_references.context: In his magnum opus, Ibn Khaldun discussed the concept of daulat, which he defined as the political authority and organization that ruled over a people. He traced its origins to the Bedouin tribes of the Arabian Peninsula and pointed out that the caliphs of the early Islamic state in Medina were the first to rule with the title daulat al-islam (the authority of Islam). This title was thereafter adopted by the Umayyads and Abbasids, and was used by the Ottoman sultans as well.

historical_references.reference: Historical records show that Al-Maqrizi's Al-Mawā'iz wa l-ī'tibār bi-dhikr al-khiṭāṭ wa l-āthār The name Daulat carried significant weight in that era.
historical_references.context: Al-Maqrizi, in his major work Al-Mawā'iz wa l-ī'tibār bi-dhikr al-khiṭāṭ wa l-āthār, wrote about the caliphs of the Islamic Empire and their territories. He made frequent references to the concept of daulat, which he described as the authority and territory governed by an Islamic ruler. He noted that the term was first used by the Umayyads, and that it came to signify the power and glory of the Islamic state.

modern_usage.modern_context: The term 'Daulat' in modern context refers to the political, administrative, and territorial authority in the Islamic world. It is seen on various platforms including political parties, government institutions, and international organizations. In the context of political parties, Daulat can be understood as the ultimate goal of establishing an Islamic state, where Sharia law is implemented. In the context of government institutions, Daulat signifies the sovereign power and authority of the state, ensuring the welfare and security of its citizens. Lastly, in the context of international organizations, Daulat represents a collective political and administrative entity, working towards the betterment and cooperation of the Muslim world.
